title: Scheme ampleness characterized by the canonical section-algebra Proj map
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Say $L$ is $f$-ample if, for every affine open $V\subseteq T$, $L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; quasi-compactness of $f$ is part of this notion. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $L$ is $f$-ample; (2) $f$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and, for the canonical graded algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes n}$ [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], the relative Proj $P=\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj], and the evaluation map $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n}$, one has $U(\psi)=X$ and $r_{L,\psi}:X\to P$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Here $f^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], $f_*N(V)=N(f^{-1}(V))$, and $U(\psi),r_{L,\psi}$ are the generation locus and canonical map of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] on schemes. The algebra and map in (2) are formed only after its quasi-separatedness condition is imposed; the algebra is then quasi-coherent. Equivalently, this algebra is $f_*(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n})$ with the grading by tensor degree. Moreover, either condition implies that $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: Assume (1). For an affine open $V\subseteq T$ put $W=f^{-1}(V)$ and $f_V:W\to V$. Affine opens of $V$ are affine opens of $T$, so $f_V$ is quasi-compact; $V$ is affine and $L|_W$ is ample by (1). Apply [lem-trf-affine-base-ample-canonical-data] to $(f_V,L|_W)$: $f_V$ is separated, its canonical section algebra $\mathcal A_V$ is quasi-coherent with evaluation $\psi_V$, $U(\psi_V)=W$, and $r_V:W\to\operatorname{Proj}_V(\mathcal A_V)$ is an open immersion.

The $f_V$ of step 1 are the restrictions of $f$ over the open covering of $T$ by all affine opens, and they are separated; hence $f$ is separated [lem-sfb-separated-lfp-target-open-locality], so quasi-separated [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated].

Apply [lem-trf-canonical-proj-open-cover-gluing] to the quasi-compact separated $f$, $N=L$, the covering of $T$ by its affine opens and the local data of step 1. It gives the quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$ with evaluation $\psi$, $U(\psi)=X$, and $r:X\to P$ an open immersion. With step 2 this is (2).

Under either (1) or (2), $f$ is qcqs (step 2, resp. hypothesis). Apply [lem-trf-qcqs-line-section-algebra-evaluation]: $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent, the comparison $\mathcal A\simeq f_*(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n})$ is a graded isomorphism, and over every affine $V$ one has $\mathcal A(V)=\Gamma_*(W,L|_W)$, $P\times_TV=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal A(V))$, with $r|_W$ the canonical section-ring map.

Conversely assume (2). For affine $V\subseteq T$, put $W=f^{-1}V$, $M=L|_W$, and $A=\mathcal A(V)$. Condition (2) makes $r_V$ an isomorphism onto an open $O\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(A)$; step 4 ([lem-trf-qcqs-line-section-algebra-evaluation]) identifies it with the canonical section-ring map. Quasi-compactness of $f$ makes $W$ and $O$ quasi-compact, and $U(\psi)=X$ gives the positive-section cover. Thus [lem-trf-proj-canonical-map-twist-comparison] supplies $d>0$ with $r_V^*\mathcal O(dk)\simeq M^{\otimes dk}$ for all $k>0$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ, (4) implies (1), affine restriction and twist comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample] to the quasi-compact open $O$: choose $e>0$ so that $\mathcal O_O(ek)$ is invertible ample for every $k>0$. Use $k=d$ here and $k=e$ in step 5. Then $M^{\otimes de}$ identifies with the ample sheaf $\mathcal O_O(de)$ under the isomorphism $W\simeq O$. The isomorphism transports its sections, nonvanishing opens, and their affineness, so the ample-sheaf definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] gives ampleness of $M^{\otimes de}$ on $W$. Any section of $(M^{\otimes de})^{\otimes n}$ is a section of $M^{\otimes den}$ with the same nonvanishing open. Since $de>0$, the same affine section cover therefore proves that $M$ is ample. This uses the easy positive-power-to-original direction directly and never assumes $\mathcal O(1)$ invertible.

The preceding argument proves $L|_{f^{-1}(V)}$ ample for every affine open $V\subseteq T$. Along with the standing quasi-compactness of $f$, this is (1). Applying steps 1--2 again gives the additional separatedness conclusion under (2) as well.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01VH, 01VI, 01VJ, equivalence (1) and (5); forward: derive separation, then qcqs pushforward and affine canonical charts; reverse: (4) implies (1).
